blocks.text: Let's solve this one step by step. The quantity negative six, squared, minus four times two times negative three.
Exponent first. Negative six squared is thirty-six, because the parentheses include the negative sign.
Now multiply left to right. Four times two is eight, and eight times negative three is negative twenty-four.
Subtracting negative twenty-four is the same as adding twenty-four. Thirty-six plus twenty-four is sixty.
Watch out for these traps. If you forget the parentheses on negative six, you get negative twelve. If you lose the negative sign on the three, you get twelve.
